recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. No core source follow-up is needed for FHIR-31573 unless Pharmacy reopens the broader MedicationStatement effective/adherence timing model.
issue_request: FHIR-31573 was a Published Pharmacy issue with resolution Not Persuasive with Modification. It reported that MedicationStatement.effective[x] still referred to the removed MedicationStatement.taken element and requested R5 wording that refers to the adherence attribute instead.
initial_application: The 2021 Pharmacy application commit 7453f87bfcb5eeba6020113412508cb95e5d4f0a, merged by 5ed2dbc90d8375e1713ec39e2310df3c052e927d, included F31573 and changed the then-current MedicationUsage.effective[x] definition from status NotTaken wording to adherence Not Taking wording.
additional_context: FHIR-38682 later renamed MedicationUsage back to MedicationStatement in b2032629f28b8d31b9a67b46170dde873398fb0d while preserving the adherence-based definition. MedicationStatement is active in source/fhir.ini, and later related reconciliations for FHIR-37372 and FHIR-32858 adjusted nearby comments without changing the FHIR-31573 definition. Direct Zulip and Confluence searches found no conflicting FHIR-31573 community record.
reconciliation: Published an empty no-change audit commit. The active StructureDefinition and mapping exception already refer to MedicationStatement.adherence Not Taking, and targeted searches found no current stale reference to MedicationStatement.taken or status NotTaken in the MedicationStatement effective definition.
